## Comparability caveats first

**Alaska is not cleanly comparable to the other four.** Alaska's FY2024 consolidated results include Hawaiian Airlines only from the September 18, 2024 acquisition date forward — roughly 3.5 months — contributing $869M of revenue and a $113M net loss [DOC-2]. So Alaska's FY2024 blends a stand-alone carrier with a partial-year, loss-making acquisition (plus whatever integration costs run through the cost lines), and its ratios are neither a true stand-alone Alaska result nor a full-year combined result.

**All five are otherwise on the same basis:** calendar-year FY2024 10-K filings, Jan 1–Dec 31 [DOC-1], so no fiscal-year mismatch exists among Delta, United, Southwest, and American.

**Metric limitation:** the data provides only two cost lines (fuel and labor) plus operating income [DOC-1] — there is no ASM/capacity data, so unit cost (CASM) cannot be computed. What follows is cost-as-a-share-of-revenue, which is influenced by stage length and network mix (Southwest's short-haul domestic model burns more fuel and labor per revenue dollar than Delta's long-haul/international and premium-heavy mix) as well as by pricing power, not by cost discipline alone.

## The numbers

| Airline | Fuel % of rev. | Labor % of rev. | Fuel+labor % | Operating margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | 17.1% | 26.2% | **43.4%** | **9.7%** |
| United | 20.6% | 29.2% | 49.8% | 8.9% |
| American | 21.1% | 29.6% | 50.6% | 4.8% |
| Alaska* | 21.4% | 30.6% | 51.9% | 4.9% |
| Southwest | 21.1% | 44.5% | 65.7% | 1.2% |

Delta: revenue $61,643M, fuel $10,566M, labor $16,161M, operating income $5,995M [DOC-1]. United: $57,063M / $11,756M / $16,678M / $5,096M [DOC-1]. American: $54,211M / $11,418M / $16,021M / $2,614M [DOC-1]. Alaska: $11,735M / $2,506M / $3,588M / $570M [DOC-1]. Southwest: $27,483M / $5,812M / $12,240M / $321M [DOC-1].

## Conclusion

Delta leads on every available measure: the lowest fuel burden (17.1% vs. 20.6–21.4% for the rest), the lowest labor burden (26.2%), the lowest combined fuel-plus-labor load (43.4%, a ~6.4-point advantage over second-place United), and the highest operating margin (9.7%) [DOC-1]. The ranking of Delta above United above American is robust across all four metrics. Southwest is the clear laggard, with labor alone consuming 44.5% of revenue and an operating margin of just 1.2% [DOC-1]. Alaska's fourth-place showing should be treated as provisional given the Hawaiian consolidation [DOC-2].

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines — lowest fuel (17.1%) and labor (26.2%) as a share of revenue, lowest combined fuel+labor load (43.4%), and highest operating margin (9.7%) of the five; note Alaska's figures are distorted by the partial-year Hawaiian consolidation from 9/18/2024, and no ASM/unit-cost data is available to control for stage-length and network-mix differences.
